sup:70740.text:
Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below.

We are delighted to present our competitive quote for your requirements. Our price is €6.10 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel of 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. Please note that AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost, while PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost. This offer remains valid for 30 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Seidl
Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

Dear customer,
Thank you very much for your message - it is always a pleasure to hear from you, and we are glad to help wherever we can.
We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows.
Our terms: a price of €5.40 per unit, Zahlungsziel 45 days net, a contract term of 24 months, a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404.
Here is the background.
We checked the index change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account.
We checked the delivery record data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation.
AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. That remains.
LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost. That remains.
PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost. That remains.
We acknowledge the recent decrease in the AS-14404 alloy surcharge and have adjusted our pricing accordingly.
We can support your request for a 24-month contract and 45-day payment terms, but this requires an AS-14404 index clause to manage long-term volatility.
With this structure in place, we propose a revised price of €5.50 per unit.
Alternatively, with a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404: €5.50 per unit.
Our price follows our main cost drivers: AS-14404, PPI-C2431, LCI-C.
We can offer a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404, AS-14404, AS-14404.
We look forward to doing good business together, and our team is always there for you.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Seidl
Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

move.text:
Dear customer,

We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows. We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account. 

We can present our current Angebot at a price of €5.40 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a contract term of 24 months, and a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404. To provide you with a more competitive base price, we must maintain the payment terms at 45 days rather than extending them to 90 days. Alternatively, with Zahlungsziel 45 days net: a price of €5.40 per unit, a contract term of 24 months, and a Preisgleitklausel on AS-14404. 

Our standard Zahlungsziel is 30 days net. A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the price. Which volume can you commit to? Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Seidl
Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

decisions.tactician: Among the options that keep two years of fixed pricing, o5 has the lowest C, a fraction below E0 and o1. Every option is about equally hard for the supplier to accept, so the choice comes down to C. A twenty-four-month term avoids the large repricing cost of a twelve-month deal (o7, o12) without the extra lock-in of thirty-six months, which earns nothing. The clause options cost us more. Leaving out the clause it asked for keeps the clause in reserve as a concession for later rounds. The two index-decline facts undercut its cost-increase argument.

decisions.tactician: o8 gives the supplier the clause it asked for, but with a 3 % deadband so the clause costs us far less than E0's zero deadband. It also adds 90 d payment, which the supplier values in cash terms. It has the lowest C of all the clause options (€242,083 vs E0's €242,312). The no-clause options score slightly lower on C, but they ignore the supplier's main stated need and are more likely to draw a hard counter. Citing our rising volume (a1) speaks to its focus on customers with volume.

The 36 months it offers costs us nothing in C, since our horizon is 2 years, and it meets the supplier's stated interest in committed volume. That makes up for its -4.5 % cash value, a figure that does not count contract length. Accepting €5.40 now would leave about €12k on the table, and the supplier has not issued a final offer, so we keep pushing.
